questions.topic: A cursor and an offset after a row above the page is deleted
questions.learningObjective: Explain why offset pagination drifts after a deletion
questions.stem: Chef Ana pages a costing sheet with OFFSET 20, then a row above the page is deleted before the next request. Why does the next page skip a row?

answer.exemplar: Offset counts physical rows from the start, so deleting a row above shifts every later row up by one and the fixed offset skips the row that moved into the deleted slot. A cursor keyed on a stable column avoids this drift because it resumes after a value rather than a count.

questions.explanation: Offset pagination is positional, so any insert or delete above the window shifts the window. The skipped row is the one that slid into the removed position, not a data loss in storage. Cursor pagination fixes this by anchoring to a value.
